meta.title: Open 2D Studio — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Open 2D Studio: a 2D CAD program for building drawings with gridlines, walls, beams, dimensions, sheets and IFC export. Succeeded by Open CAD Studio; the web version can still be tried.

header.label: 2D CAD · succeeded by Open CAD Studio
header.title: Open 2D Studio
header.tagline: 2D drafting for construction, continued in Open CAD Studio
header.desc: Open 2D Studio was a 2D CAD program for building drawings, with gridlines, walls, beams, dimensions, sheets and IFC export. The last version came out in March 2026; Open CAD Studio is its successor. The web version remains available to try.

alt.drawing: Open 2D Studio in the dark theme: a floor plan with gridlines, a slab, a stair, curved and straight beams and the ribbon with drawing and modify tools
alt.ifc: The Open 2D Studio IFC dashboard with the spatial structure of project, site, building and storeys, listing the walls, beams, spaces and gridlines per storey
alt.standards: The Drawing Standards window with gridline dimensioning and the hatching per material, such as concrete, masonry, calcium silicate, timber and steel

notice.text: Succeeded by Open CAD Studio. Open 2D Studio no longer gets new versions. The web version stays online for now; installers and source code are not publicly available. The images come from a demo video of a development build.

features.label: Features
features.heading: 2D building drawings, with an IFC model behind them
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

draw.title: Drafting the way you know from CAD
draw.desc: Lines, arcs, polylines, circles, ellipses and text, with snapping to the grid and to objects, layers and a command line. Move, copy, rotate, mirror, offset, trim and fillet, with undo and redo.

aec.title: Gridlines, walls, beams and slabs
aec.desc: Draw with building objects instead of loose lines: gridlines with automatic dimensions, walls with openings, beams with labels and a profile search, slabs and columns. Levels in a section belong to the storeys of the project.

standards.title: Hatching per material
standards.desc: Set the hatching per material, such as concrete, masonry, calcium silicate, timber and steel, with pattern, angle, spacing and colour. In the same drawing standards you set the dimensioning of gridlines.

ifc.title: An IFC model next to the drawing
ifc.desc: What you draw goes into an IFC4 model with project, building and storeys. The IFC dashboard shows the spatial structure and the STEP file, and you export the model as IFC. You can sync the model with Bonsai in Blender.

shapes.title: Drawing tools
shapes.desc: Line, rectangle, circle, arc, polyline, spline, ellipse, hatch, image and text.

modify.title: Modify
modify.desc: Move, copy, rotate, scale, mirror, array, offset, trim, extend, fillet and chamfer.

annotate.title: Dimensions and text
annotate.desc: Linear, aligned, angular, radius and diameter dimensions, leaders and text styles.

snap.title: Snapping and layers
snap.desc: Snap to grid, endpoint, midpoint, centre and intersection; layers with visibility, lock and colour.

command.title: Command line
command.desc: Type commands as in CAD, next to the ribbon.

grid.title: Gridlines
grid.desc: Gridlines with bubbles and automatic dimensions per scale.

walls.title: Walls and openings
walls.desc: Walls with end caps and openings you can move.

beams.title: Beams, columns and slabs
beams.desc: Straight and curved beams with labels, columns per storey and slabs with a top-level label.

sections.title: Sections and levels
sections.desc: Levels in a section stay linked to the storeys of the project.

hatch.title: Hatch patterns
hatch.desc: Hatching per material and a pattern manager of its own.

sheets.title: Sheets and title blocks
sheets.desc: Sheets with scaled viewports and title blocks.

pdf.title: Print and PDF
pdf.desc: Print drawings or export them as PDF.

queries.title: Schedules and quantities
queries.desc: SQL queries on the model data for schedules and quantities.

ifc.title: IFC export
ifc.desc: An IFC4 model with storeys and a dashboard with the spatial structure.

bonsai.title: Bonsai sync
bonsai.desc: Sync the IFC model with Bonsai in Blender.

api.title: Scripts, API and MCP
api.desc: A scripting API, a local HTTP API and an MCP server for AI assistants.

ext.title: Extensions
ext.desc: Extensions with their own ribbon buttons and dialogs, such as Drawing Statistics.

whatsnew.label: New in v0.35.0
whatsnew.title: The last version: gridlines, levels and themes
whatsnew.desc: Released on 26 March 2026; no newer version followed. What was added since v0.32.0.

grid.title: Gridlines and dimensions
grid.desc: Automatic dimensions at the bubbles, extension per scale and grips to drag dimensions.

levels.title: Levels and storeys
levels.desc: A level in a section updates the storey, also when you move or copy it.

walls.title: Openings in walls
walls.desc: Openings you can move, and end caps on walls.

beams.title: Beam labels and profiles
beams.desc: Labels on beams and a search in the profile library.

themes.title: Themes
themes.desc: Choose the interface theme, such as dark.

blender.title: Bonsai sync
blender.desc: Sync the IFC model with Bonsai in Blender.

status.q: Is Open 2D Studio still being developed?
status.a: No. The last version, v0.35.0, came out in March 2026. Open CAD Studio is its successor: a CAD program for 2D and 3D with DWG and DXF support.

use.a: The web version still runs in the browser, without installing anything. There will be no new versions or fixes; for new work Open CAD Studio is the better choice.

download.q: Why can I not get the desktop app?
download.a: The installers and the source code are in a repository that is not public. If you are looking for a CAD program for your computer, install Open CAD Studio.

files.q: Which files can it read and write?
files.a: Its own project file (.o2d), DXF for reading and writing, and IFC and PDF for export.

move.q: Can I take my drawings to Open CAD Studio?
move.a: Export them from Open 2D Studio as DXF and open that file in Open CAD Studio. Building objects then come along as an ordinary drawing.

cost.a: Nothing. The web version is free to use, without an account.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: For those who want to know how it is built.

tauri.title: Tauri 2 and Rust
tauri.desc: The desktop app, with DXF import and export and a local HTTP API in Rust.

react.title: React and TypeScript
react.desc: The interface with ribbon, panels and dialogs.

canvas.title: Canvas 2D
canvas.desc: Its own renderer with a QuadTree for fast selection.

state.title: Zustand and Immer
state.desc: Separate state per open file, with undo through patches.

ifc.title: web-ifc
ifc.desc: Creating and reading the IFC model in the app.

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.desc: Drawing commands for AI assistants, next to the scripting API.

cta.status: Open 2D Studio no longer gets new versions. The drafting work continues in Open CAD Studio.
